core_obligations: Reduce to the affine case X = Spec(A) with A Noetherian, and note that U is quasi-compact, hence U = D(f_1) union ... union D(f_n) for finitely many f_i (proof lines 453-457).

Translate the three conditions: scheme theoretic density of U becomes injectivity of A -> A_{f_1} x ... x A_{f_n}; condition (3) becomes: for every associated prime p of A some f_i does not lie in p; condition (2) becomes density together with containment of the embedded points (proof lines 458-462).
Prove (1) implies (3): if a in A has annihilator a prime p, then a is nonzero, so its image in some A_{f_i} is nonzero, giving f_i not in p (proof lines 465-468).

Prove (2) and (3) are equivalent: U is dense in Spec(A) exactly when it contains all minimal primes, and the associated primes of A are the union of the minimal primes and the embedded associated primes (proof lines 471-476).

Prove (3) implies (1): if every associated prime p corresponds to a prime of some A_{f_i}, then A -> A_{f_1} x ... x A_{f_n} is injective because A -> product over p in Ass(A) of A_p is injective (proof lines 479-484).
proof_roadmap: Localisation to X = Spec(A), Noetherian, and finiteness of the cover U = D(f_1) union ... union D(f_n) (proof lines 453-457).
Rewriting of the three conditions in the ring A (proof lines 458-462).
(1) implies (3) via the annihilator of an element (proof lines 465-468).
(2) equivalent to (3) via minimal primes versus embedded associated primes (proof lines 471-476).
(3) implies (1) via injectivity of A into the product of the localisations at the associated primes (proof lines 479-484).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states a three-way equivalence for an open subscheme U of a locally Noetherian X: scheme theoretic density, density plus containment of all embedded points, and containment of all associated points (statement lines 443-449). The work is a reduction plus an algebraic re-reading: the author first passes to X = Spec(A) with A Noetherian, uses quasi-compactness of U to write it as D(f_1) union ... union D(f_n), and then replaces the geometric conditions by statements about the single ring map A -> A_{f_1} x ... x A_{f_n} and about the associated primes of A (proof lines 453-462). The two non-obvious steps are reading density as containment of the minimal primes and invoking that the associated primes are exactly the minimal primes together with the embedded ones (proof lines 471-476), and closing the cycle by the injectivity of A into the product of its localisations at the associated primes (proof lines 479-484). This is H2: standard localisation machinery, but four separate implications, each needing its own translation rather than a citation.

compared: public 469 (tag 0573, more-morphisms-lemma-scheme-theoretically-dense-generic-fibre) uses the notion of scheme theoretic density in a generic fibre and spreads it over an open subset of the target; it neither characterises density by associated or embedded points nor proves the three-way equivalence of the present card.

public 467 (tag 0GSI) and public 470 (tag 05F1) are about relative associated points and fibre-dimension behaviour along specialisations for flat or finite-type morphisms; they do not characterise scheme theoretic density of an open subscheme.

public 269 (tag 0BJZ, local-cohomology-lemma-check-finiteness-pushforward-on-associated-points) and public 270 (tag 0AWA) use associated points to decide coherence of a pushforward along an open subscheme; the statement there is about finiteness and Hartogs extension, not about density.

public 587 (tag 0BEM, varieties.tex) mentions embedded points only as a nuisance to be removed before turning an Euler characteristic into a polynomial; it contains no criterion for an open subscheme to be scheme theoretically dense.
